title: 測量実習・演習Ⅰ
subtitle: Surveying Practicum / Exercises I
keywords: Distance, Degree, Bearing 2.Error, Precision 3.Total Station 4.Distance survey, Control point survey 5.Declination survey, Leveling survey
educationalGoal: (1) Practice the surveying methods learned in Surveying I and Surveying II (2) Practice distance, control point, leveling and declination surveys and reports. (3) Reports are equivalent to company reports. Students will learn how to create data in required formats. (4) Students who master the topics in Surveying I/II and Surveying Practicum I/II will have the skills necessary for an Assistant Surveyor national license.
advice: Surveying Practicum / Exercises I will be carried out as active learning practice based on “Total Ability” learning in the CLIP learning process. (1) Distance Surveying Students learn the basics of distance surveying including measuring distances by pacing, using steel tape, fabric tape and TS, and will compare the accuracy of each. (2) Total Station (TS) equipment Students learn how to use TS equipment and its internal programs. (3) Angle Surveying Students learn the basics of angle surveying using TS equipment, including how to set control points and conduct declination surveys. (4)Leveling Surveys Students learn how to use auto levels and electrical levels, practice small-scale direct leveling and master profile leveling and rise-fall leveling recording methods. (5)Advice Materials in Moodle are useful for practice and for creating reports. The schedule is subject to change depending on the weather. The first class is Zoom. Reference the e-syllabus for the latest information of class relating Covid-19.
requiredKnowledge: Surveying Practicum / Exercises I builds on the contents of Surveying I and II with practical skills. Students must fully understand lecture content from the Surveying I and II courses. High-level courses, Surveying II, Surveying Practicum / Exercises II, and Spatial Information Engineering are also offered, along with other surveying-related courses such as Environmental Civil Engineering Experiments B and Spatial Information Design Exercises.

achievementLevels.ideal: Distance Surveying: Students clear standard achievement levels and can report measurements using steel tape, fabric tape and pacing in order of accuracy. Total Station: Students clear standard achievement levels and can perform advance fixing using high-level programs. Angle surveying: Students clear standard achievement levels and can conduct highly accurate angle surveying. Leveling: Students clear standard achievement levels and can conduct highly accurate leveling. Students can lead practical training and play a central role in their groups.
achievementLevels.standard: Distance Surveying: Students understand surveying methods, data calculation and accuracy. Total Station: Students understand the basic use of Total Station methods. Angle surveying: Students can install and operate total station programs and can perform angle surveying. Leveling: Students understand the installation of auto levels and electronic levels with certainty and can carry out leveling. They can use profile leveling and rise-fall leveling recording methods. Students can use equipment introduced in classes thus far.
